behavior.summary: The day-30 mismatch stems from conflicting requirements between the operations handbook and migration ticket. The operations handbook (line 3) states "Returns are accepted through day 30" — an inclusive boundary (≤30 days). The migration ticket (line 3) states "Allow returns before day 30" — an exclusive boundary (<30 days). Legacy-v1 implements the handbook's inclusive rule (eligible at age_days=30), while rewrite-v2 implements the ticket's exclusive rule (ineligible at age_days=30). This is not an off-by-one error but a deliberate requirement change: the migration ticket redefines the window from inclusive to exclusive. All other cases (day-29, day-31, missing-receipt, final-sale) match, confirming the boundary is the only difference.

policy.summary: The two artifacts define conflicting policies for the 30-day return window. The operations-handbook (line 3) states "Returns are accepted through day 30," which implies day 30 is inside the window (age_days <= 30). The migration-ticket (line 3) states "Allow returns before day 30," which implies day 30 is outside the window (age_days < 30). The legacy-v1 baseline matches the handbook (day 30 eligible), while rewrite-v2 matches the ticket (day 30 outside_window). Since the handbook is typically the authoritative operations document, the approved policy per the handbook is that day 30 is inside the return window.

regression.summary: This is an intentional policy change, not a regression. The operations handbook (line 3) states "Returns are accepted through day 30" — an inclusive boundary (≤30 days) that matches legacy-v1 behavior (day-30 eligible). The migration ticket (line 3) states "Allow returns before day 30" — an exclusive boundary (<30 days) that matches rewrite-v2 behavior (day-30 outside_window). The test matrix confirms only the day-30 boundary differs (day-29 and day-31 match). Since the migration ticket explicitly redefines the window from inclusive to exclusive, the rewrite correctly implements the new documented requirement. This is a deliberate requirement change, not an unintended behavioral shift.
